title: Tools, and how to connect them
hook: From no tools, to function calling, to MCP servers. The model decides, your code does.
inPlainWords: A tool is a function the model can ask your software to run, like "look up order" or "issue refund". The model asks. Your code does the work and returns the result.

useCase.title: Answer "Where is my order #48213?"
useCase.story: The answer lives in the order system, not in any document, and it changes hourly.

approaches.name: No tools
approaches.what: The model answers only from text it has seen.
approaches.avoidWhen: Any live data. It will guess.
approaches.example: The bot says "It should arrive soon!" for every order.

approaches.name: Hard-coded lookup
approaches.what: Your code detects order numbers and always calls the order system.
approaches.example: If the message has # and digits, call the order API.

approaches.name: Tool calling (function calling)
approaches.what: You describe tools. The model chooses which to call and with what inputs. Your code runs them.
approaches.avoidWhen: Tools that can do harm without checks.

approaches.name: MCP servers
approaches.what: Tools are packaged behind a shared standard, so any compatible AI app can use them.
approaches.greatWhen: Many tools, several apps, or reuse across teams.
approaches.example: An "orders" server used by the chat bot, an internal assistant and a coding tool.

approaches.name: Screen control
approaches.what: The model clicks through screens like a person.
approaches.avoidWhen: Anything that has an API. It is slower and more fragile.
approaches.example: Filling in a form on a legacy carrier website.

challenge.question: The bot must answer live order status accurately. What do you add?

options.why: Live data comes from the source, and read-only means it cannot change anything by mistake.

options.text: Paste the order database into the prompt
options.why: Huge, stale immediately, and a privacy problem.
Old orders do not tell you where today's parcel is.

options.text: A screen-control agent on the admin site
options.why: It can work, but it is slow and fragile when a proper API exists.

bestCase.title: A real lookup tool with limited permissions
bestCase.example: "Where is order 48213?" The model calls get_order_status(48213), gets "Out for delivery, arriving today", and tells the customer exactly that. The tool is read-only, so it cannot alter anything.

worstCase.title: Letting it guess, or giving it a tool with too much power
worstCase.example: With no tool, the bot says "Should arrive in 3 to 5 days!" for an order that was already delivered. Or an all-powerful admin tool lets a confused model cancel the wrong order.

steps.label: Model picks a tool
steps.goesWrong: There is no tool available, so the model guesses "3 to 5 days".

steps.label: Your code runs it
steps.goes: It calls the order system with read-only access.

steps.label: Model replies
steps.goes: "Your order is out for delivery and should arrive by 6pm."

takeaway: The model decides. Your code does. Give every tool the least power it needs.
